GNU Info is a second help system, built like a hyperlinked book.

A man page is a short leaflet about one command. An Info document is a whole textbook about a software package. It has links, an index, and a search across the entire document. Many core tools, such as the
libraries, come from the GNU Project and use Info. Some tools have both; the Info version is usually deeper. The comparison stops at paper: Info can also be turned into other formats.

There are two systems because of how open source communities developed over the years. Man pages are formal and cover one command or function each, as separate text files. Info documents cover a whole package, include more practical examples, and are hypertext. Learn both so you can use whichever helps most.
